objective:
Let the `stockroom` command read its input files from standard input, so that it can sit at the end of a shell pipeline.

Wherever a command option names an input file (`items --file`, `stock --items`, `stock --stock`, `sales --orders`, `price --items`), the value `-`, exactly that one character, means standard input. The whole of standard input, decoded as UTF-8 text with line ends normalised the way reading a file in text mode does, is used as the text of that file, and the command behaves exactly as if a file with that content had been named. Any other value stays a path: `./-` names a file called `-` in the current directory. The global option `--config` does not take standard input: `--config -` names a settings file called `-` in the current directory and fails as any missing settings file does when there is none.

Standard input can be read only once. When `-` is given for more than one input option of a single command (for example `stock --items - --stock -`), the command ends with exit code 1 and stderr holds the one line `stockroom: error: <reason>` where the reason contains the words `standard input`; nothing is written to stdout. Empty standard input is an empty file: `items --file -` with no input fails the same way `items --file` of an empty file does. Everything else about the command line, the output and the exit codes is unchanged.
acceptance: With '-' as the file, items, stock (either of --items and --stock, with the other one a normal file), sales (also with --from) and price read the text from standard input and print exactly what they print for a file with the same content
Standard input is decoded as UTF-8 and handled like a text-mode file: non-ASCII names come through and a CRLF input gives the same output as the same content in a file
'-' given for both --items and --stock of stock ends with exit code 1, empty stdout and one 'stockroom: error: ' line on stderr that contains 'standard input', whatever standard input holds
Empty standard input gives the same exit code, stdout and stderr as an empty file does, for items and for sales
Only the exact value '-' means standard input: './-' reads the file called '-' in the current directory
'--config -' reads the settings file called '-' in the current directory (and is an error when there is none); it never reads standard input
Paths that are not '-' still work, and the exit codes and messages of runs that do not use '-' are unchanged
